chunk_findings.detail: The `_CI_TIMEOUT` regex scans the whole command string for the first `--timeout N`, so it mistakes a nested subprocess timeout (or a `--timeout` embedded in another argument value) for the `ddflow ci run` queue budget. For example, with `cfg.ci.suite_wait_s = 1800`, `queue_budget_s("ddflow ci run -- pytest --timeout 120", cfg)` returns `120` instead of `1800`, and `queue_budget_s('ddflow ci run --description "use --timeout 1800" --timeout 3600', cfg)` returns `1800` from the description string instead of `3600`. In `runner.py` the first case makes the gate timeout `run_timeout + 120` rather than `run_timeout + 1800`, so a run that legitimately queues more than 120 seconds for the suite lock is killed before its real budget begins.
chunk_findings.title: `ddflow/services/workers.py:queue_budget_s`

chunk_findings.detail: The new regression test only exercises standalone `--timeout` flags such as `ddflow ci run --timeout 3600`; it does not cover the nested/embedded `--timeout` case above. Because of that gap the regex parsing bug in `queue_budget_s` passes the suite undetected. A test like `assert WK.queue_budget_s("ddflow ci run -- pytest --timeout 120", c) == 1800` would fail on the current implementation.
chunk_findings.title: `tests/test_auto_workers.py:test_a_ci_run_gets_a_queue_budget_on_top_of_its_run_timeout`

chunk_findings.detail: The test monkey-patches `GB.PF.apply` to return `("failed", "")`, so it never exercises the actual value proposition of the feature: a non-test blocker must keep the gate failed even when baseline-red would have made the test result pass. If `GB.apply` merely records `baseline_split` and returns whatever `PF.apply` returned, this test still passes. The critical input is `PF.apply` returning `("passed", "")` with `ev["checks_failed"] = ["ruff check", "unit tests"]`; in that case the test should assert `result == "failed"` because of the blocker, but the current test cannot catch a regression that ignores the blocker.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_baseline_red_auto.py:test_gate_baseline_apply_records_the_split_and_stays_failed

chunk_findings.detail: If `BL.check_split(...)` returns `None` for the natural “no split applies” case, the function falls through the `if split:` guard and executes `None.get("note", "")`, raising `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'`. The guard only protects the `ev["baseline_split"]` assignment, not the subsequent `.get()` call, so any caller that passes an `ev` with no non-test blockers (or any input for which `check_split` returns `None`) crashes the gate-result handling instead of returning an empty note and continuing with baseline-red logic.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline.py:76 (_split_note)

chunk_findings.detail: The `_HOOK_FAILED` regex `^(?P<name>.+?)\.{3,}.*?Failed\s*$` assumes the word `Failed` is the final non-whitespace token on the status line. Pre-commit colors the status word in terminals/CI when color is enabled, producing a line like `ruff check.................................................................\x1b[31mFailed\x1b[0m`. Because `\s*$` only permits whitespace after `Failed`, the trailing ANSI reset sequence `\x1b[0m` prevents a match, so `failed_checks("ruff check.................................................................\x1b[31mFailed\x1b[0m")` returns `[]` instead of `["ruff check"]`. The function therefore silently misses real hook failures whenever the environment forces pre-commit color output (e.g. `PRE_COMMIT_COLOR=always` or a TTY).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci_marker.py:44

chunk_findings.detail: `check_split` classifies a failed check as a test by the substring test `"test" in c.lower()`, so any non-test check whose id happens to contain those letters is misclassified. For example, `check_split(["attest"], tests=0)` returns `{}` because "attest" is treated as a test check, so a non-test blocker is hidden and no split is recorded. Similarly, `check_split(["latest-lint", "mypy"], tests=0)` returns `blocking=["mypy"], test_checks=["latest-lint"]`, putting a non-test blocker in the test bucket. The feature is meant to surface non-test blockers beside baseline-red tests, but this heuristic silently drops or mislabels them.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline.py:130

chunk_findings.detail: The test/non-test partition is `test_checks = [c for c in failed if "test" in c.lower()]`, but that does not match the existing policy in the same module: `only_tests_failed` also treats `c.id == "command"` as test-equivalent. Concrete input `check_split(["command"], 1)` returns `{"blocking": ["command"], ...}`, so `gate_baseline.apply` returns `failed` early and never reaches the baseline-red path, even though `only_tests_failed` says a failed `command` check is not a non-test blocker. Conversely, the pre-commit hook `name-tests-test` is a non-test validation hook but contains `"test"`, so `check_split(["name-tests-test"], 1)` returns `{}`; `_split_note` then records no `baseline_split` and returns no note, allowing the real non-test blocker to be missed while baseline-red logic proceeds. The substring test therefore mislabels both directions.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline.py:check_split

chunk_findings.detail: A red pre-commit test hook with id `pytest` is misclassified as a non-test blocker. `re.search(r"\btests?\b", "pytest", re.I)` is `None` because the substring `test` inside `pytest` is not preceded by a word boundary, so `check_split(["pytest"], 3)` returns `{"blocking": ["pytest"], ...}` instead of `{}`. In `ddflow/api/gate_baseline.py`, `_split_note` then returns `"blocked by non-test check(s): pytest; 3 failing test(s) are judged apart (baseline-red) and do not clear it"`, so the gate stays `"failed"` instead of taking the baseline-red/partial path. The pre-existing `only_tests_failed` at `ddflow/services/gates/baseline.py:124` used `"test" in c.id.lower()`, which does recognize `pytest` as a test check, so this change is a regression for a very common local pre-commit hook id.
